result.title: RMR-VLA: Recurrent Memory Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models
result.summary: Long-horizon, history-dependent robotic manipulation often requires acting on visual cues that have disappeared, such as an object indicated earlier or a target hidden under a moving cup. The key challenge is to maintain what past evidence means for the next action as the scene changes. We introduce Recurrent Memory Reasoning (RMR), an explicit reasoning step that connects memory to action inside a vision-language-action model (VLA), with no external reasoning model. At each update, the VLA first infers an event from visual evidence, then revises the task state and grounds a subgoal in the current scene to guide action generation. Carrying the state and subgoal across updates lets remembered identities and task progress determine the current target, doubling RoboMME success over an otherwise identical model without recurrence. Joint training lets one VLA both reason and act; because its memory decisions are text tokens with exact likelihoods, GRPO refines them from rollout rewards without making action generation stochastic. Among the compared methods, RMR-VLA achieves the best results on RoboMME (66.46% overall, 79.83% on the Reference category) and LIBERO-Mem (90.08%).

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RMR-VLA，在 VLA 内部加入显式循环记忆推理步骤：每次更新先从视觉证据推断事件，再修订任务状态并在当前场景中 grounding 子目标以指导动作生成；记忆决策以文本 token 表达，并用 GRPO 由 rollout 奖励优化，在 RoboMME 与 LIBERO-Mem 上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 关注的推理状态跨更新携带与视觉证据如何决定当前目标，可供核查的是状态以文本 token 而非 latent 承载、以及记忆内容被动作生成实际使用与贡献分配的程度。
